title: Climate change, sea level rise, and the agricultural revolution
abstract: arXiv:2610.37306v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We test various hypotheses for the invention and spread of agriculture: higher temperatures, increased seasonality, carbon dioxide fertilization, sea level rise, and technological progress on the extensive margin. We successfully replicate Matranga (QJE 2024). His seasonality hypothesis survives alternative data, estimators, and competing hypotheses. Population density played a role in the invention of agriculture, while spatial diffusion was important for its spread. Sea level rise and climate change had a minor effect on the population density of the areas that first adopted agriculture. Extrapolating a logit model for the invention of agriculture, some now-submerged areas in the Persian Gulf, Mediterranean, and Yellow Sea were suitable for early agriculture. Over time, technological progress was the main factor in extending agriculture's extensive margin.

translated_title: 气候变化、海平面上升与农业革命
translated_abstract: 我们检验了关于农业发明与传播的多种假说：更高的温度、增强的季节性、二氧化碳施肥效应、海平面上升，以及扩展边际上的技术进步。我们成功复制了Matranga（2024年发表于《经济学季刊》）的研究。其季节性假说在替代数据、估计方法和竞争性假说的检验下依然成立。人口密度在农业的发明中发挥了作用，而空间扩散对农业的传播至关重要。海平面上升和气候变化对最早采用农业的地区的人口密度影响较小。通过外推农业发明的logit模型，波斯湾、地中海和黄海中一些现已淹没的区域曾适合早期农业。随着时间推移，技术进步是农业扩展其广泛边际的主要因素。
tldr: 该研究验证了农业起源与传播的多种假说，发现季节性假说最为稳健，人口密度促进了农业的发明，空间扩散推动了农业的传播，而技术进步是农业扩展到新区域的主要驱动力。
en_tdlr: This study tests competing hypotheses for the invention and spread of agriculture, finding the seasonality hypothesis robust, with population density aiding agricultural invention, spatial diffusion driving its spread, and technological progress being the main factor extending agriculture's extensive margin over time.
